ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AC$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $BC$ is the chord of $\odot O$, point $P$ is a point outside $\odot O$, and $PB$ and $AB$ are connected, with $\angle PBA=\angle C$. $PB$ is the tangent of $\odot O$; connect $OP$, if $OP\parallel BC$ and $OP=8$, the radius of $\odot O$ is $3$, find the length of $BC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution:\\
Since the radius of $\odot O$ is $3$,\\
hence $OB=3$, $AC=6$,\\
Since $OP \parallel BC$,\\
thus $\angle CBO = \angle BOP$,\\
Since $OC=OB$,\\
thus $\angle C = \angle CBO$,\\
thus $\angle C = \angle BOP$,\\
Also, since $\angle ABC = \angle PBO = 90^\circ$,\\
thus $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PBO$,\\
thus $\frac{BC}{OB} = \frac{AC}{OP}$,\\
that is $\frac{BC}{3} = \frac{6}{8}$,\\
hence $BC = \boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle ⊙O; points A and C are on the circle, and line segment AC passes through the center O of the circle, and is a diameter; point B is on the circumference at the upper right of the circle, and BC and AB are chords inside the circle; point P is on the right side outside the circle, PB is tangent to the circle at point B, OP connects from the center of the circle to P, and in the figure OP is parallel to the direction of BC. Reasoning: The radius of the circle is 3, so OB=OC=3, and the diameter AC=6. Because AC is a diameter, the inscribed angle it subtends ∠ABC=90°. Because PB is the tangent to the circle at point B, the radius OB is perpendicular to the tangent PB, so ∠PBO=90°. Also because OP∥BC, ∠BOP=∠CBO. Since OB=OC, triangle OBC is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠CBO=∠OCB; and O, C, A are collinear, so ∠OCB is ∠ACB, that is, ∠C in the problem. Therefore ∠BOP=∠C. Thus △ABC and △PBO have one pair of right angles equal, and also have ∠C=∠BOP, so △ABC∼△PBO. The corresponding sides are BC↔OB, AC↔OP, therefore BC/OB=AC/OP. Substituting OB=3, AC=6, OP=8, we get BC/3=6/8, so BC=3×6/8=9/4.
